title: One Active Coverage per Home: Ownership Rule of the Calloway Limited Home Warranty
content:
**Rule.** Under the Calloway Limited Home Warranty a home carries exactly one active coverage at a time. A coverage is enrolled only for a home that has no other active coverage, except a subsequent-owner enrollment, which ends the previous owner's active coverage on the subsequent owner's deed date.

**Evidence.** The test is made on the company's coverage records before the enrollment is written: the home is identified by the purchase agreement under which Calloway sold it, and the question is whether a coverage on that same purchase agreement is currently active. What a caller says about the home's ownership does not replace that record.

| Existing coverage on the same purchase agreement | Enrollment requested | Result |
|---|---|---|
| None active | Any | May be enrolled |
| One active | Original buyer enrollment | Not enrolled; the home already has an active coverage |
| One active | Subsequent-owner enrollment | May be enrolled; the previous owner's active coverage ends on the subsequent owner's deed date |

**Retired clause.** The clause "Every owner of the home shares the same coverage start date and coverage end dates, and history that counts over the life of the coverage (missed appointments, one-time repairs) counts across owners of the same home" is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis: for the missed-appointment charge only the missed appointments recorded on the homeowner's own coverage are counted, never those recorded on a previous owner's coverage of the same home, while every owner of the home still shares the coverage start and end dates and one-time repairs still count across owners.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A home's original buyer used one drywall nail pop visit, and the home then passed to a subsequent owner. The subsequent owner's coverage carries the same coverage start and end dates as the original buyer's, and the visit already used counts against the one-time repairs of the home; a missed appointment recorded on the original buyer's coverage is not among the missed appointments counted for a missed-appointment charge on the subsequent owner's coverage.

superseded_clauses: Every owner of the home shares the same coverage start date and coverage end dates, and history that counts over the life of the coverage (missed appointments, one-time repairs) counts across owners of the same home.
